The '''Volgastani Expansionist Doctrine''' was the late twentieth-century pattern of territorial and legal claims associated with the [[Volgastan Baathist Republic]].

== Doctrine ==

The Istragarde source describes Volgastan as using treaty language about territorial integrity and cultural protection to justify aggressive border revisions. The doctrine treated weak enforcement as an opportunity: Volgastan could claim legal or historical grounds, act militarily, and then withstand symbolic condemnation.

== Istragarde Weakness ==

The [[Istragarde Tribunal]] issued repeated rulings against Volgastan, but the [[Treaty of the Concord of Istragarde]] lacked direct enforcement power. No unified military response followed, allowing Volgastan to expand influence and territory through calculated campaigns.

== Precedent And Wars ==

The treaty source presents the 1971 [[Invasion of Batravalka]] by [[Karlist Perzam]] as an important precedent. Volgastan's later doctrine followed a similar pattern of invoking historical claims, cultural protection, and treaty ambiguity.

The [[Volgastani-Osman War]] and the pre-1995 phase of the [[Volgastani-Hanovkayan War]] are preserved as likely related conflict anchors, though their detailed causes and outcomes are not yet source-confirmed.

== Source Limits ==

The source says Volgastan controlled far more territory by the mid-1990s, but this 1994-back draft stops short of defining post-1994 borders or final war outcomes.
